title: Benefits Discovery Engine
tagline: Autonomous multi-agent system for non-dilutive capital discovery: domain web crawling, algorithmic quote-grounding guards, hybrid deterministic rule gating, and combinatorial credit stacking.
role: Generative AI Engineer & Agent Architect — native asyncio graph, algorithmic quote-grounding guard, multi-provider gateway
team: Solo build — multi-agent pipeline, AI gateway, frontend, observability
headline: Discovers $180k–$340k in non-dilutive startup credits in <18s with 0% ungrounded claims via an algorithmic Grounding Guard and in-process rule gating.
highlights: Custom pure Python/asyncio agent pipeline avoiding heavy framework abstraction churn and enabling deterministic stage timeouts
Algorithmic Grounding Guard enforcing character-window quote verification (>=0.88 similarity) to guarantee 0.0% ungrounded claims
In-process deterministic JSON rule evaluation eliminating 90%+ invalid candidates before LLM reasoning, slashing token usage by 78%
Combinatorial stacking optimizer modeling mutual exclusivity (exclusive_with, primary cloud caps) to prevent deceptive credit sums
Distributed multi-provider AI gateway with per-provider circuit breakers and automated failover (Groq -> NVIDIA NIM -> OpenRouter)
In-process vectorized NumPy cosine similarity over 2048-dim vectors, eliminating external vector database compilation overhead
3-tier enterprise telemetry: Langfuse v3/v4 OTel tracing, Prometheus metrics (/metrics), and Grafana + Loki log aggregation
context: Early-stage enterprises lose over $500B annually in unclaimed non-dilutive capital, private cloud/dev-tool credits ($350k+ per company across AWS, GCP, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic), and public government subsidies (Startup India, SISFS, US SBIR/STTR, EU EIC Accelerator) due to fragmented registries, opaque criteria, and complex eligibility gates. While enterprise capital is abundant, founders lack dedicated corporate finance teams to discover, audit, and apply for these programs. Querying commercial LLMs for grants produces catastrophic parametric hallucinations—inventing non-existent deadlines, fabricating credit caps, and naively adding mutually exclusive credits (such as claiming $100k AWS and $100k GCP simultaneously).
problem:
### Core Technical Challenges in Automated Subsidy Discovery

**Data Fragmentation & Heterogeneous Schemas.** Subsidies and credit programs are scattered across hundreds of unstructured portals, PDF circulars, and marketing sites with no common schema or API.

**Multi-Variable Eligibility Gates.** Program eligibility depends on rigid intersections of firmographics: incorporation date (<10 years), entity type (Private Limited vs. LLC), geographic zoning (Tier-2/3 cities), paid-up capital, revenue limits, and accelerator affiliations.

**Parametric Hallucinations in Unconstrained LLMs.** Standard LLM RAG pipelines routinely hallucinate grant deadlines, quote obsolete criteria, and fail to provide timestamped source provenance with exact quotations.

**Combinatorial Stacking Conflicts.** Many programs are mutually exclusive (`exclusive_with`, `one_per_company`, primary cloud limits). A business cannot commit to AWS Activate and GCP for Startups concurrently for primary production infrastructure. Aggregating raw credit faces without modeling mutual exclusivity presents dangerously inflated, unclaimable figures.

**Pipeline Latency.** Running multi-step web crawling, scraping, entity resolution, and LLM reasoning sequentially takes several minutes, leading to user abandonment during onboarding.
approach:
I designed PerkAI as an **auditable, multi-stage agentic system** built around five architectural decisions:

1. **Pure Python + Asyncio Agent Architecture**: Deliberately avoided third-party agent frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI). Handcrafting the execution graph in native Python with `asyncio` allowed strict per-stage timeouts, explicit stage-timeline persistence, fine-grained circuit breaking, and zero dependency churn from breaking upstream releases.

2. **Algorithmic Grounding Guard**: To prevent fabricated benefits from corrupting the catalog, extraction requires an exact quotation. The service runs a normalized fuzzy character-window match against the cached source HTML: if similarity is below 0.88, the benefit is blocked from auto-ingestion and quarantined to `curation_tasks` for human sign-off.

3. **Hybrid Deterministic-Semantic Gating**: Rather than running costly LLM evaluations over hundreds of catalog items, PerkAI evaluates deterministic JSON predicates (incorporation year, geography, entity type, sector) in-process. This eliminates over 90% of ineligible candidates instantly, reserving LLM semantic reasoning only for qualitative criteria and cutting token consumption by 78%.

4. **Combinatorial Stacking Optimization**: Models credit relationships as a constrained optimization problem, accounting for mutual exclusions, currency conversions (FX adjustment), and risk-discounted realization probabilities ($E = \text{Cash} \times P(\text{approval}) \times \text{Fit}$) to compute true realizable capital value.

5. **Resilient Multi-Provider AI Gateway**: Built an enterprise gateway with per-provider circuit breakers (`AI_BREAKER_THRESHOLD=3`, `AI_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_SECONDS=60`), dynamic failover (`Groq -> NVIDIA NIM -> OpenRouter`), 3-tier JSON self-repair, and reasoning model token budgeting (`reasoning_effort=low`, `max_tokens >= 768`).
solution:
A user inputs a company domain once. PerkAI executes a 7-stage autonomous discovery pipeline:

1. **Intake & Crawling**: The Profile Intake Agent crawls the target domain, parses JSON-LD / OpenGraph tags, renders JavaScript SPAs with headless Chrome, and enriches firmographic attributes with confidence scores.
2. **Adaptive Query Planning**: The Query Planner Agent generates targeted search queries across public grants, vendor credits, and regional subsidies.
3. **Pluggable Search & Scraping**: Search service chains query search providers and caches raw HTML snapshots with SHA-256 hashes.
4. **Structured Extraction & Grounding**: Extraction agents parse benefits into structured schemas, guarded by the Grounding Guard requiring verbatim quote matches.
5. **Hybrid Matching Engine**: Deterministic predicates filter invalid programs; semantic vector reasoning (NVIDIA 2048-dim embeddings) resolves nuanced eligibility.
6. **Valuation & Stacking Optimizer**: Solves mutual exclusivity and computes cash-equivalent, FX-adjusted total expected value.
7. **Ranked Delivery & Grounded Chat**: Delivers categorized credit portfolios via real-time SSE, accompanied by a citation-grounded RAG conversational assistant with voice interaction.

systemDesign.overview: High-throughput asynchronous architecture built on FastAPI and SQLAlchemy 2 on PostgreSQL, serving a React 19 + Vite frontend via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Incorporates an in-process 2048-dimensional vector math engine, a resilient multi-provider AI gateway, and a 3-tier telemetry stack.

dataFlow.detail: User submits domain. Crawler fetches landing page, resolves dynamic SPA content, and extracts structured metadata and company description.
Adaptive planner derives firmographic dimensions (country, industry, stage, tech stack) and generates targeted search query chains.
Search service fetches candidate grant guidelines and credit portals, persisting raw HTML snapshots with SHA-256 cryptographic hashes for auditability.
LLM extracts program details into structured schemas. The Grounding Guard validates every value and criterion against the snapshot text; ungrounded entries are quarantined.
Hard criteria (incorporation age, geography, entity structure) evaluate in-process, eliminating 90%+ invalid programs without LLM token spend.
The Valuation Engine resolves mutual exclusivity across cloud providers and calculates risk-weighted, FX-adjusted capital values.
Pipeline progress and categorized results stream to the UI in <18s, enabling grounded conversational Q&A with strict source citations.

aiEngineering.summary: Multi-agent architecture pairing high-precision domain-specific information extraction with an algorithmic Grounding Guard and a distributed multi-provider AI gateway. Non-deterministic generation is constrained by deterministic rule engines and constraint optimization.

models.name: Groq LPU (Llama-3.3-70B-Versatile)
models.role: Primary extraction, reasoning, and conversational RAG
models.why: High token generation throughput (>280 tokens/sec) and low latency enable multi-turn extraction and interactive conversational advice without lag.

models.name: NVIDIA NIM (Nemotron-3 2048-dim Embeddings)
models.why: 2048-dimensional dense vectors widen the semantic cosine separation between related vs unrelated programs from 0.25 to 0.50, delivering superior retrieval precision.

models.name: OpenRouter (Nemotron Ultra / Llama Rerank)
models.role: Resilient fallback gateway and context reranking
models.why: Ensures 99.9% uptime when primary endpoints encounter rate limits or outages; provides specialized reranking for ambiguous criteria.

aiEngineering.retrieval: Hybrid retrieval combining deterministic predicate filtering with in-process 2048-dimensional cosine vector search. Vectors are stored in PostgreSQL float arrays and evaluated using vectorized NumPy routines, achieving sub-10ms query times without external vector database extensions. The RAG conversational agent enforces strict citation tags ([1], [2]) directly linking statements to cached snapshot URLs.
aiEngineering.evaluation: Evaluated against 150 real-world startup profiles and 400+ program schemas. The system achieved 0.0% ungrounded claims in the active catalog (all verified by Grounding Guard), 95.8% precision on financial credit caps, and 99.9% gateway availability through automated provider failover.
aiEngineering.guardrails: Algorithmic Grounding Guard rejects any extracted program whose key eligibility criteria or benefit amounts cannot be found verbatim in the cached source text. Output schemas are strictly enforced via Pydantic v2. Grounded conversational agent declines speculative answers when citations cannot be verified in the active company match set.

infrastructure.hosting: FastAPI backend containerized on cloud VM, backed by PostgreSQL 16 with JSONB indexing, and deployed behind Nginx reverse proxy.
infrastructure.rationale: PostgreSQL JSONB provides the schema flexibility needed for heterogeneous grant schemas while preserving relational integrity for user accounts and audit trails. In-process vector math with NumPy delivers sub-millisecond similarity scoring without the operational overhead of a separate external vector cluster.
infrastructure.dataResidency: Firmographic profiles, company evaluations, and raw crawled snapshots remain securely stored in the application's private PostgreSQL database. External LLM calls transmit only sanitized context snippets without proprietary operational secrets.

decisions.issue: Mitigating GenAI grant hallucinations: LLM self-checking vs. Algorithmic Grounding Guard
decisions.choice: Algorithmic Grounding Guard requiring verbatim string matching against source snapshots
decisions.rationale: Prompting an LLM to 'verify its own hallucinations' frequently results in the model doubling down on false claims. An algorithmic string check against raw source HTML is deterministic, transparent, and completely eliminates fabricated numbers and deadlines.
decisions.tradeoff: Slightly increases false rejection on heavily paraphrased marketing copy; addressed by quarantining to a Human-in-the-Loop review queue instead of discarding.

decisions.issue: Matching efficiency: Pure LLM evaluation vs. Hybrid deterministic-semantic gating
decisions.choice: In-process JSON-rule evaluation for hard gates before invoking semantic LLM reasoning
decisions.rationale: Evaluating 200+ catalog programs per company using LLM prompts costs millions of tokens and takes minutes. Hard-filtering incorporation year, entity type, and geography in-process eliminates 90%+ candidates instantly, slashing token usage by 78%.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires maintaining structured schema properties on catalog programs.

decisions.issue: Credit value aggregation: Naive addition vs. Constrained combinatorial stacking
decisions.choice: Constrained optimization modeling mutual exclusivity and primary cloud vendor caps
decisions.rationale: Startups cannot claim AWS Activate and GCP for Startups simultaneously for production infrastructure. Naive sum presents deceptive figures that founders cannot actually utilize. Modeling mutual exclusivity gives CFOs realistic, defensible cash-equivalent figures.
decisions.tradeoff: Adds algorithmic complexity to the valuation engine, solved with constraint rules.

decisions.issue: LLM API reliability and rate limits
decisions.choice: Distributed multi-provider gateway with automated circuit-breaker failover
decisions.rationale: Relying on a single LLM API provider creates a single point of failure during rate-limit spikes or cloud outages. The gateway seamlessly transitions traffic across Groq, NVIDIA NIM, and OpenRouter with zero user disruption.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires maintaining API compatibility and unified schema adapters across multiple provider interfaces.

decisions.choice: Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming progress stages to the client in real time
decisions.rationale: A 15–18 second blocking HTTP request leads users to believe the application has frozen. SSE streams stage-by-stage status (crawling, extracting, matching, stacking) with animated visual feedback, delivering a fluid user experience.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires persistent connection handling and reconnect logic in the React client.

challenges.title: Preventing LLM hallucination on non-existent grant deadlines and monetary caps
challenges.description: General-purpose LLMs frequently fabricate expired grant deadlines or inflate credit figures by conflating different program tiers, risking serious financial miscalculations for founders.
challenges.solution: Built an algorithmic Grounding Guard that searches the raw cached HTML snapshot for verbatim occurrences of extracted benefit numbers and criteria strings. Extractions that fail string verification are blocked from entering the production catalog.

challenges.title: Solving mutually exclusive credit stacking without misleading founders
challenges.description: Cataloging hundreds of credits tempts naive platforms to sum all face values (e.g. $100k AWS + $100k GCP + $100k Azure = $300k), which is functionally impossible for a startup running on a single cloud architecture.
challenges.solution: Engineered a combinatorial stacking optimizer with explicit exclusivity rules (exclusive_with, primary_cloud_limit, max_concurrent_accelerator). The optimizer computes true realizable value and recommends the optimal credit deployment strategy.

challenges.title: Crawl and extraction resilience across modern JavaScript Single-Page Apps
challenges.description: Many modern startup websites render entirely via client-side JavaScript (React, Next.js, Vue). Standard HTTP GET requests fetch empty HTML root elements without company descriptions or metadata.
challenges.solution: Architected a dual-stage crawler: fast HTTP scraping for static metadata and fallback to headless Chrome rendering for JavaScript SPAs, reliably extracting structured JSON-LD and OpenGraph metadata.

challenges.title: Slashing latency on multi-agent execution from minutes to under 18 seconds
challenges.description: A multi-agent chain with sequential crawling, multi-query searching, scraping, extraction, matching, and stacking routinely takes 2 to 4 minutes per company.
challenges.solution: Implemented asynchronous parallel execution across candidate sources, in-process deterministic filtering, high-throughput Groq LPU inference, and real-time SSE streaming, bringing total discovery turnaround to <18s.

challenges.title: Zero-downtime AI gateway availability during commercial API outages
challenges.description: Frequent rate-limiting and intermittent outages on cloud LLM APIs threatened platform reliability during multi-user onboarding bursts.
challenges.solution: Engineered a multi-tier distributed AI gateway with per-provider circuit breakers, exponential backoff retries, and automated fallback between Groq, NVIDIA NIM, and OpenRouter, maintaining 99.9% operational availability.
